Explicit methods approximate solutions of initial value problems

\[
y' = f(t,y), \qquad y(0)=y_0
\]

by stepping forward from the initial condition. This app compares Euler's method, Improved Euler's method, and the classical fourth-order Runge--Kutta method.

```{ojs}
    .split(",")

    .filter(Boolean)
  return selected.length ? selected : methodOptions
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
improvedEulerSolve = function(f, a, y0, b, n) {
  const h = (b - a) / n
  const points = [{ x: a, y: y0 }]

  let t = a
  let y = y0

  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const k1 = f(t, y)
    const yPredict = y + h * k1
    const k2 = f(t + h, yPredict)
    y = y + (h / 2) * (k1 + k2)
    t = a + (i + 1) * h
    points.push({ x: t, y })
  }

  return points
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
result = {
  try {
    const f = VM.expressions.makeFunction2(math, committed.fText)
    const y0Value = VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, committed.y0Text)
    const bValue = VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, committed.bText)

    if (!Number.isFinite(y0Value)) {
      throw new Error("The initial value y0 must be a finite number.")
    }

    if (!Number.isFinite(bValue)) {
      throw new Error("The endpoint b must be a finite number.")
    }

    if (bValue <= 0) {
      throw new Error("The endpoint b must be greater than 0.")
    }

    const n = Math.max(1, Math.round(committed.n))
    const maxNValue = Math.max(1, Math.round(committed.maxN))

    const trueTrajectory = VM.numerical.rk4Solve(f, 0, y0Value, bValue, 2000)
    const trueValue = trueTrajectory[trueTrajectory.length - 1].y

    return {
      ok: true,
      f,
      y0: y0Value,
      b: bValue,
      n,
      maxN: maxNValue,
      trueTrajectory,
      trueValue
    }
  } catch (error) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      message: error.message
    }
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
setup = {
  if (!result.ok) return null

  const { f, y0, b, n, maxN, trueTrajectory, trueValue } = result

  const eulerTrajectory = VM.numerical.eulerSolve(f, 0, y0, b, n)
  const improvedTrajectory = improvedEulerSolve(f, 0, y0, b, n)
  const rk4Trajectory = VM.numerical.rk4Solve(f, 0, y0, b, n)

  const eulerValue = eulerTrajectory[eulerTrajectory.length - 1].y
  const improvedValue = improvedTrajectory[improvedTrajectory.length - 1].y
  const rk4Value = rk4Trajectory[rk4Trajectory.length - 1].y

  const iterates = Array.from({ length: maxN }, (_, i) => {
    const currentN = i + 1

    const euler = VM.numerical.eulerSolve(f, 0, y0, b, currentN)
    const improved = improvedEulerSolve(f, 0, y0, b, currentN)
    const rk4 = VM.numerical.rk4Solve(f, 0, y0, b, currentN)

    const eulerEnd = euler[euler.length - 1].y
    const improvedEnd = improved[improved.length - 1].y
    const rk4End = rk4[rk4.length - 1].y

    return {
      n: currentN,
      euler: eulerEnd,
      improved: improvedEnd,
      rk4: rk4End,
      eulerError: Math.abs(eulerEnd - trueValue),
      improvedError: Math.abs(improvedEnd - trueValue),
      rk4Error: Math.abs(rk4End - trueValue)
    }
  })

  return {
    eulerTrajectory,
    improvedTrajectory,
    rk4Trajectory,
    trueTrajectory,
    eulerValue,
    improvedValue,
    rk4Value,
    trueValue,
    iterates
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mainPlot = {
  if (!result.ok) return html`<div class="alert alert-danger">${result.message}</div>`

  const traces = []

  traces.push({
    x: setup.trueTrajectory.map(p => p.x),
    y: setup.trueTrajectory.map(p => p.y),
    mode: "lines",
    name: "Reference solution",
    line: { color: "black", width: 3 }
  })

  if (showEuler) {
    traces.push({
      x: setup.eulerTrajectory.map(p => p.x),
      y: setup.eulerTrajectory.map(p => p.y),
      mode: "lines+markers",
      name: "Euler's method",
      line: { color: "#d62728", width: 2 }
    })
  }

  if (showImprovedEuler) {
    traces.push({
      x: setup.improvedTrajectory.map(p => p.x),
      y: setup.improvedTrajectory.map(p => p.y),
      mode: "lines+markers",
      name: "Improved Euler",
      line: { color: "#ff7f0e", width: 2 }
    })
  }

  if (showRK4) {
    traces.push({
      x: setup.rk4Trajectory.map(p => p.x),
      y: setup.rk4Trajectory.map(p => p.y),
      mode: "lines+markers",
      name: "RK4",
      line: { color: "#1f77b4", width: 2 }
    })
  }

  const allY = traces.flatMap(trace => trace.y).filter(Number.isFinite)
  const yRange = VM.plotting.paddedRange(allY)

  return Plotly.newPlot(
    DOM.element("div"),
    traces,
    {
      title: "Approximate solutions",
      xaxis: { title: "t" },
      yaxis: { title: "y", range: yRange },
      margin: { t: 50, r: 20, b: 50, l: 60 },
      legend: { orientation: "h" }
    },
    { responsive: true }
  )
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
valueTable = {
  if (!result.ok) return html``

  const rows = []

  if (showEuler) {
    rows.push({
      Method: "Euler's method",
      [`Approximation to y(${result.b})`]: setup.eulerValue,
      "Absolute error": Math.abs(setup.eulerValue - setup.trueValue)
    })
  }

  if (showImprovedEuler) {
    rows.push({
      Method: "Improved Euler",
      [`Approximation to y(${result.b})`]: setup.improvedValue,
      "Absolute error": Math.abs(setup.improvedValue - setup.trueValue)
    })
  }

  if (showRK4) {
    rows.push({
      Method: "RK4",
      [`Approximation to y(${result.b})`]: setup.rk4Value,
      "Absolute error": Math.abs(setup.rk4Value - setup.trueValue)
    })
  }

  rows.push({
    Method: "Reference",
    [`Approximation to y(${result.b})`]: setup.trueValue,
    "Absolute error": 0
  })

  return VM.ui.renderTable(rows)
}
```

```{ojs}
valueTable
```

Euler's method uses the slope at the beginning of each step. Improved Euler averages a beginning slope and an estimated ending slope. RK4 combines four slope evaluations per step and is usually much more accurate for the same step size.

## Examples

The examples below show how explicit methods behave on different initial value problems. Euler's method is simple but low-order, Improved Euler is more accurate, and RK4 usually tracks the reference solution closely with far fewer steps.

Click any example to load it into the app.

```{=html}

  <a class="example-card" href="?f=y%20-%20t%5E2%20%2B%201&y0=0.5&b=2&n=4&max=20&show=euler,improved,rk4">
    <div class="example-card-title">Textbook nonlinear forcing</div>
    <div class="example-card-formula">y' = y - t^2 + 1, &nbsp; y(0)=0.5</div>
    <div class="example-card-text">A standard test problem where the three explicit methods can be compared against a smooth reference solution.</div>
  </a>

  <a class="example-card" href="?f=t%20-%20y&y0=1&b=5&n=6&max=40&show=euler,improved,rk4">
    <div class="example-card-title">Relaxation toward a trend</div>
    <div class="example-card-formula">y' = t - y, &nbsp; y(0)=1</div>
    <div class="example-card-text">The solution is pulled toward the increasing trend t, showing how step size affects lag and accuracy.</div>
  </a>

  <a class="example-card" href="?f=y*(1%20-%20y)&y0=0.1&b=8&n=8&max=60&show=euler,improved,rk4">

    <div class="example-card-formula">y' = y(1-y), &nbsp; y(0)=0.1</div>
    <div class="example-card-text">A bounded nonlinear growth model where the solution rises quickly and then levels off near the carrying capacity.</div>
  </a>

  <a class="example-card" href="?f=-2*y&y0=3&b=4&n=5&max=40&show=euler,improved,rk4">
    <div class="example-card-title">Exponential decay</div>
    <div class="example-card-formula">y' = -2y, &nbsp; y(0)=3</div>
    <div class="example-card-text">A simple decay problem that highlights numerical damping and the effect of using larger time steps.</div>
  </a>

  <a class="example-card" href="?f=2*y&y0=0.25&b=2&n=4&max=40&show=euler,improved,rk4">
    <div class="example-card-title">Exponential growth</div>
    <div class="example-card-formula">y' = 2y, &nbsp; y(0)=0.25</div>
    <div class="example-card-text">A rapidly increasing solution where low-order errors grow along with the solution.</div>
  </a>

  <a class="example-card" href="?f=sin(t)%20-%200.5*y&y0=0&b=10&n=12&max=80&show=euler,improved,rk4">

    <div class="example-card-formula">y' = sin(t) - 0.5y, &nbsp; y(0)=0</div>
    <div class="example-card-text">A forced system with oscillation and damping, useful for seeing how the methods track changing slopes.</div>
  </a>

  <a class="example-card" href="?f=y%5E2%20-%20t&y0=0&b=2&n=8&max=50&show=euler,improved,rk4">

    <div class="example-card-formula">y' = y^2 - t, &nbsp; y(0)=0</div>
    <div class="example-card-text">A nonlinear example where curvature changes over the interval and higher-order methods gain a visible advantage.</div>
  </a>

  <a class="example-card" href="?f=-10*(y%20-%20cos(t))%20-%20sin(t)&y0=1&b=3&n=6&max=80&show=euler,improved,rk4">

    <div class="example-card-formula">y' = -10(y - cos(t)) - sin(t), &nbsp; y(0)=1</div>
```
